product.name: netMind Extension
product.description: AI browser agent — chat with pages, automate tasks, multi-provider LLM support.

services._whyBackendBaseUrl: netMind Extension backend (deploy/netmind_extension_backend): verifies the Viettel SSO ID token and issues the LiteLLM model key. Replaces the former Second Brain service.
services._whyLitellmBaseUrl: Fallback only. The backend returns an authoritative baseUrl on every provision and that value wins, so this matters just for a client that has a key but has not provisioned yet. Already ends in /v1, so nothing is appended.
services._whyOidcEndpoints: The Viettel SSO wrapper publishes no /.well-known/openid-configuration, so the two endpoints discovery would have supplied are named here. Set both or neither.
services._whyOidcIdTokenAlg: The wrapper signs ID tokens with HS256 and serves no JWKS, so the extension cannot check the signature. Pinning the header alg at least refuses a token swapped to `none` or to an alg this deployment never issues.
services._whyOidcBearerToken: Which token the backend can verify. With the provider fully named in this config, sign-in never consults the backend's /api/auth/providers — this value alone decides what gets sent, so it must match how the backend verifies (the advertised bearer_token only reaches installs whose config names no provider). The wrapper signs ID tokens with a secret it gives nobody, so the backend verifies by calling the wrapper's /userinfo instead — and /userinfo recognises only the opaque access token it minted, answering 401 'Token not found or expired' for an ID token that was never in any store to be found. Set back to id_token the day the wrapper publishes a JWKS and the backend checks signatures locally again.
services._whyOidcSendNonce: The Viettel SSO wrapper does not echo the `nonce` back in the ID token, so sending one guarantees a failed sign-in: OIDC Core §3.1.3.7 requires the client to reject a token whose nonce does not match what it sent. `nonce` is OPTIONAL for the authorization code flow, so not sending it is spec-clean — unlike sending one and skipping the check. This DOES give up a layer of replay protection; PKCE S256, the verified `state`, and an ID token that arrives over the back channel rather than the browser redirect carry the rest. Set this back to true the day the wrapper echoes the nonce.

replacements._why: Temporarily shield upstream API header names from display-name replacement.

Upstream sells a hosted tier next to the extension, so its provider is labelled "WebBrain Cloud". netMind has no such split — the managed gateway is simply what the product runs on — and letting the rule below rename only the first word leaves "netMind Extension Cloud" in the model picker. Must stay ahead of that rule, which would otherwise consume the WebBrain half first. Only the two-word display name is matched: the provider id webbrain_cloud, api.webbrain.one and the X-WebBrain-* headers carry no space and are untouched.
Display name in UI and skill text. Guards keep it out of identifiers and protocol tokens such as ensureWebBrainGroup and X-WebBrain-Help-Improve.
Restore upstream API header names after display-name replacement.
Lowercase brand name inside translated sentences. Scoped to locale files only; the lookarounds keep it off webbrain.one, webbrain_note and webbrain-tools.
Fallback prefix for downloaded screenshot filenames.
User-visible export and capture filenames.
Fallback names for recordings and staged screenshots.
Branded workflow exports while continuing to import legacy WebBrain and AgentX WebMate workflow files.
Accept new, previous-brand, and legacy workflow file extensions.
Send reviews and feedback to the product repository until store listings are available.
Do not show a misleading store-review prompt before netMind Extension has official listings.
Send feedback to the product issue tracker.
Point the in-app documentation link to this repository's documentation.
Avoid promoting the upstream brand in localized social-share copy.

Vietnamese is the default UI language. Upstream picks the browser language and falls back to English; netMind ships to Vietnamese users whose browsers are mostly en-US, so a saved choice wins and everyone else starts in Vietnamese.
Default locale in exported/imported config, so a config round-trip does not reset the UI to English.
Locale the background worker assumes for the selection shortcut before the user picks one.
Locale the background worker assumes for the selection shortcut before the user picks one (Firefox build).
Selection-shortcut strings fall back to Vietnamese instead of English for unknown locales.
The in-page selection bubble renders before the background answers with the stored locale; start it in Vietnamese instead of the browser language.
Vietnamese heads the language picker, matching the default locale. Paired with the rule below, which drops the entry from its alphabetical slot at the end.
